page.content:
The FIA world championship — constructors, circuits, and the drivers who own weekends.

How Formula 1 connects

  • Faction: FIA — The FIA governs Formula 1 and awards its world championships.
  • Item: World Drivers' Championship — The World Drivers' Championship is Formula 1's individual title.
  • Item: World Constructors' Championship — The Constructors' Championship is Formula 1's team title.
  • Event: Monaco Grand Prix — The Monaco Grand Prix is Formula 1's street-circuit classic.
  • Faction: Scuderia Ferrari — Ferrari is the only constructor present since the first World Championship.
  • Event: British Grand Prix — The 1950 British Grand Prix at Silverstone opened the World Championship.
  • Event: 1994 San Marino Grand Prix — Senna's death at Imola forced Formula 1's modern safety revolution.
  • Faction: Formula One Group — The Formula One Group sells the championship as a global television product.
  • Concept: Hybrid era — The hybrid era is the 2014-onwards regulations chapter of Formula 1.
  • Event: Italian Grand Prix — The Italian Grand Prix is Ferrari's home Formula 1 race.
  • Event: British Grand Prix — The British Grand Prix is the championship's founding race.
  • Faction: Mercedes-AMG Petronas — Mercedes-AMG Petronas is the hybrid-era factory team.
  • Faction: Red Bull Racing — Red Bull Racing is the constructor of the Vettel and Verstappen dynasties.
  • Faction: McLaren — McLaren is the British constructor of the Senna–Prost era.
  • Location: Spa-Francorchamps — Spa-Francorchamps is a drivers' favorite on the Formula 1 calendar.

What is Formula 1?

Formula 1 is the FIA World Championship that began in 1950. Its lore runs through Ferrari, McLaren, Mercedes, and Red Bull; through Monaco, Monza, and Silverstone; and through Senna, Schumacher, Hamilton, and Verstappen.

Key threads lead to FIA, World Drivers' Championship, World Constructors' Championship, Monaco Grand Prix, Scuderia Ferrari and British Grand Prix.
